name: Mailchimp
tagline: Email marketing platform with campaigns, automations, forms, and analytics

pricing.notes: Official pricing page checked; 2026 public coverage lists Standard starting at $20/month for small contact counts, with subscriber-based scaling and discounts/promos.

verdictSummary: A campaign sender is buildable, but Mailchimp's value is deliverability, templates, compliance, automations, segmentation, ecommerce integrations, and support.
coreLoopDIY: Build subscriber lists, campaign composer, templates, segmentation, sends via SES/Postmark/Mailgun, unsubscribe and analytics.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because email is business-critical and deliverability problems are expensive.

priorArt.name: Mautic
priorArt.desc: Open-source marketing automation platform with email campaigns and contact management.

alternatives.name: Brevo Free
alternatives.desc: Campaigns, forms and automation with many contacts but only 300 daily sends.

facts.install: Hosted signup, sender verification, and optional domain authentication
facts.dataFormat: Contacts, campaigns, templates, automation events, and reports live in Brevo's cloud; exports are available, but the internal storage format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: Brevo's free 300-email daily ceiling makes a single larger campaign slower than Mailchimp and its free emails carry Brevo branding.
facts.setupBlocker: The first meaningful hurdle is verifying the sender and setting SPF/DKIM records for a sending domain; without that, deliverability will disappoint.

alternatives.name: EmailOctopus Free
alternatives.desc: A real small-list plan with forms and simple automations; reports expire after thirty days.

facts.install: Hosted signup, list import, and sender/domain verification
facts.dataFormat: Subscribers, campaigns, forms, automation state, and reports live in EmailOctopus's cloud; CSV import/export is supported, while the internal storage format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: Free-plan reports expire after 30 days and the account is limited to one landing page or form, leaving less history and experimentation than Mailchimp.
facts.setupBlocker: A sender address must be verified, and serious sending should use an authenticated domain.

alternatives.name: MailPoet Starter
alternatives.desc: Campaigns, forms, analytics and basic automation inside WordPress; the free list stops at 500.

facts.install: Install the WordPress plugin, create a MailPoet account, and enter the free Starter-plan key
facts.dataFormat: Lists, subscribers, newsletters, forms, and settings live in MailPoet tables inside the site's WordPress database; MailPoet's sending service processes recipient addresses and keeps delivery logs, which its documentation says are erased after three months.
facts.gapVsPaid: It works only inside WordPress and the free Starter allowance stops at 500 subscribers and 5,000 emails per month.
facts.setupBlocker: It requires an existing, maintained WordPress site plus a plan key and sender/domain approval; it is not a standalone email app.

alternatives.name: Mautic
alternatives.desc: The heavyweight open-source replacement for segmentation and automation; it also replaces ease with operations.

facts.install: Download the production package or install with Composer, then configure PHP, a database, cron, and a mail transport
facts.dataFormat: Contacts, segments, campaigns, events, and reports live in the configured MySQL or MariaDB database; assets, configuration, logs, and queue files live on the server filesystem.
facts.gapVsPaid: Mautic offers more control but gives up Mailchimp's managed deliverability, upgrades, templates, integrations, and low-maintenance operation.
facts.setupBlocker: The first wall is not the installer but production operation: PHP and database tuning, several cron jobs, HTTPS, backups, upgrades, SMTP/API sending, and DNS authentication.

alternatives.name: Notifuse
alternatives.desc: A modern visual campaign and automation stack; you own the database and the deliverability chores.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or one application container plus PostgreSQL for self-hosting
facts.dataFormat: Self-hosted contacts, campaigns, automations, and events live in PostgreSQL; files can use S3-compatible storage, and the configured email provider receives message payloads. Hosted data lives in Notifuse's cloud.
facts.gapVsPaid: Notifuse has a smaller template and integration ecosystem, and self-hosters assume database, upgrade, deliverability, and sending-provider work that Mailchimp handles.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting still needs Docker, PostgreSQL, a public HTTPS endpoint, an SMTP or API sending provider, and correctly authenticated sending domains.

alternatives.name: Plunk
alternatives.desc: Campaigns, transactional mail and workflows together; audience CRM depth is thinner.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or the official Docker Compose stack
facts.dataFormat: The self-hosted stack stores core data in PostgreSQL, jobs and cache in Redis, and objects in MinIO; hosted data is kept in Plunk's EU infrastructure.
facts.gapVsPaid: Plunk's audience CRM, template ecosystem, campaign analytics, and non-technical marketing workflow are noticeably thinner than Mailchimp's.
facts.setupBlocker: Hosted use still needs domain authentication; self-hosting adds PostgreSQL, Redis, MinIO, Nginx or another proxy, exposed web and SMTP services, DNS, and ongoing deliverability work.

alternatives.name: Sender Free
alternatives.desc: Campaigns, forms, analytics and unlimited workflows in a useful free tier; the monkey can retire.

facts.install: Hosted signup, list import, and sender/domain verification
facts.dataFormat: Subscribers, campaigns, forms, automation state, transactional messages, and analytics live in Sender's cloud; the internal storage format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: Sender's one-seat branded free plan has a smaller integration and template ecosystem than Mailchimp, even though its send allowance is generous.
facts.setupBlocker: The first real hurdle is authenticating the sending domain and warming a legitimate list rather than merely creating the account.

rejectedAlternatives.name: listmonk
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Campaigns and forms are excellent, but the missing automation builder is not a footnote here.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Mailchimp Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free plan now stops at 250 contacts and omits automation flows; the mascot is mostly a signup form.

rejectedAlternatives.name: SendPortal
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A familiar open-source recommendation with no commit since April 2024.

notes: Classic hidden-moat example: the UI can be rebuilt; inbox placement cannot be hand-waved.
prompt:
Build me a small-list email campaign tool to replace Mailchimp. Requirements:

- Node + Express + better-sqlite3 on my VPS. Admin UI bound to localhost/VPN; only
  the subscribe and unsubscribe endpoints are public.
- Contacts with tags and custom fields, CSV import and export, and segments saved
  as filters (has tag X, joined after date, opened last campaign).
- Campaigns written in Markdown, rendered into one clean single-column HTML email
  with mjml, plain-text alternative generated automatically.
- Send through Amazon SES (keys in .env) with throttling and per-recipient status;
  SES bounce and complaint notifications auto-suppress those addresses.
- Compliance baked in: unsubscribe link and postal address in every footer, a
  List-Unsubscribe header, double opt-in on the public signup form.
- Open tracking is a per-campaign toggle, default off. Campaign report shows sent,
  bounced, and unsubscribed counts.
- One SQLite file holds everything; no telemetry, no third-party trackers.
- Out of scope: the drag-and-drop template editor, automation journeys, and
  ecommerce integrations. One good template, sent well.
- README warning: inbox placement is earned, not coded. Document SPF, DKIM, and
  DMARC setup and tell me to warm up sending volume gradually.
